Source contracts: src/agent_runtime/permission_policy.py

src/agent_runtime/permission_policy.py

Python · Tier A

Define and evaluate deterministic user permission policies independently of tool enablement and hard runtime safety. Typed rules cover Skills, tools and supported executable/subcommand families; helpers normalize precedence, evaluate concrete operations and construct proposed grants. Trusted authority owners validate one-shot confirmation and persist grants; this module performs no storage or execution.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
SkillPermissionRule 81 User decision for every tool owned by one canonical Skill. The policy normalizer optionally checks that Skill against the installed registry; a narrower tool or Shell rule may take precedence.
ToolPermissionRule 89 User allow/ask/deny decision for one canonical tool identity, independent of whether that tool is selected or currently available.
ShellPermissionRule 98 User decision for an executable and optional supported structural subcommand prefix. Arbitrary argument values and script contents are not reusable rule identities; exact operations use separate approval handling.
ShellPermissionRule.structural_family 108 Validate each prefix token against the declared executable/subfamily vocabulary. Unsupported argument-like prefixes raise; an empty prefix remains an executable-wide rule, including for otherwise unknown programs.
AgentPermissionPolicy 128 Versioned user permission snapshot with Manual, Custom, Full Access or Deny mode. Default confirmation behavior applies to operations classified as needing confirmation; explicit rules can also restrict otherwise read-only operations. Capability selection, hard safety and credentials are separate checks.
AgentPermissionPolicy.exact_version 141 Require the exact integer schema version 1 before coercion and reject booleans, strings or unsupported versions.
AgentPermissionPolicy.canonical_rules 152 Deduplicate rules by stable identity, reject conflicting decisions and sort their serialization. Non-Custom modes reject explicit rules and derive their fixed confirmation decision from the selected mode.
PermissionGrant 182 Validated user grant request targeting a run/prompt, conversation or global scope with an optional expected revision. Exactly one rule or full policy is required; a rule grant must allow the matching pending operation.
PermissionGrant.allow_only 193 Reject missing or simultaneous rule/policy payloads and non-Allow rule grants. A full policy is validated by its own schema; matching the pending operation and scope revision is the authority layer's responsibility.
rule_identity 210 Construct the canonical Skill, tool or executable/subcommand key used to deduplicate, replace and identify matched permission rules. It contains the structural rule identity, not arbitrary invocation arguments.
normalize_permission_policy 221 Revalidate supplied models/dictionaries and optionally reject unknown Skill/tool identities against the registry. None selects Manual defaults; Shell rule syntax is validated by its own schema without probing executables.
effective_permission_policy 242 Select the first non-null complete policy from prompt, conversation and global scopes. Only when all are absent, derive the legacy Manual/Full Access fallback from context; no sparse merging occurs.
apply_permission_policy 256 Write the canonical permission snapshot and corresponding legacy approval mode into the mutable execution context. Only Full Access maps to full_access; Custom and Deny retain manual while their policy carries the actual rule decisions.
PermissionDecision 270 Immutable allow/ask/deny result with the optional matched rule identity and an explanatory reason, consumed by execution authorization and its diagnostic projections.
evaluate_permission 288 Evaluate user permission after hard safety succeeds, preferring tool rules over Skill rules and longest matching Shell prefixes per parsed command. For command chains use the strongest decision; opaque syntax cannot silently bypass restrictive Shell rules. A trusted exact confirmation can override user Ask/Deny but never the early hard-safety rejection. This function trusts confirmation provenance established by the authority layer.
grant_matches 401 Check whether a proposed allow rule covers the pending tool, its owning Skill, or every parsed Shell command signature. Opaque Shell syntax and a Shell rule for a non-Shell invocation return false rather than granting a broad exception.
with_permission_grant 427 Return a canonical Custom policy that replaces only the same rule identity with the granted rule, preserving other rules and the inherited confirmation default. This builds policy data; persistence and concurrent-revision checks belong to the authority.
permission_suggestion 440 Suggest an allow rule for the exact non-Shell tool or the longest recognized family of a single literal Shell command. Return None for opaque/multiple commands, hidden subcommands or general- purpose interpreters; suggestions are not themselves authorization.
